songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Telepathic Dark Star, soaring Eleven and epic Other One suite
ai_show_review.blurb: The concert opens with a telepathic Dark Star that segues into Saint Stephen, The Eleven and Turn On Your Lovelight. Highlights include the sprawling Other One suite, an extended Alligator jam, and a heartfelt Death Don't Have No Mercy. Pristine soundboard capture makes this Fillmore West run stand out.
ai_show_review.review: March 2, 1969 marked the final night of the Grateful Dead’s legendary Fillmore West marathon, and the band delivered a performance that still feels fresh. The set kicks off with an otherworldly Dark Star—Jerry’s tone shimmering on the left channel while Phil locks in a telepathic bass groove—then rockets through Saint Stephen, The Eleven (a rhythmic marvel driven by Bill Kreutzmann’s sublime drumming) and a rapturous Turn On Your Lovelight. The second set unfolds as a tapestry of improvisation: Cryptical Envelopment weaves into an expansive Other One suite, punctuated by the haunting “Death Don't Have No Mercy,” while the Alligator jam stretches out with relentless energy before winding down through Caution, Feedback and a gently floating And We Bid You Good Night. Tom Constanten’s keyboard work adds a tender, almost classical texture that brightens the Dark Star and underpins many of the jams, making this night uniquely psychedelic. With lossless 16‑track soundboard sources that capture every nuance—crisp vocals, balanced instrument separation and only minor cuts—the recording stands as one of the most vivid documents of the Dead’s early improvisational peak.

best_recording.reason: Excellent lossless soundboard capture with pristine mix, clear instrument separation and only minor cuts.

key_highlights: Telepathic Dark Star that launches the show into a soaring improvisational journey.
The Eleven delivers one of Bill Kreutzmann’s finest rock drum performances ever captured.
Epic Other One suite paired with an extended Alligator jam showcases peak group chemistry.
Tom Constanten’s tender, psychedelic keyboard textures add a unique flavor to the set.
song_highlights: And We Bid You Good Night

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is perfect and his counterpoint on Dark Star feels telepathically beautiful, staying in lockstep with Phil throughout.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides a solid, ever‑present bass foundation that locks tightly with the drums during The Eleven and the extended jams.
band_performance.Brent: Tom Constanten’s keyboard work shines—tender, playful and unusually psychedelic—adding fresh textures to Dark Star and the jam sections.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann delivers a sublime, rock‑driving performance that anchors the high‑energy improvisations.

must_listen_sequences: And We Bid You Good Night
